The sort and its dispositions hold. The log design is sound: one file, one entry per card, and a card leaves the board only after its entry is committed. I would change three things.

- **Guard (b):** "a triggered experiment not taken up or dropped" can't be checked mechanically, because triggers like "next story touching the file" are prose. Give each entry a machine-matchable trigger key, such as a file path or card tag, so a checker can fire without false positives.
- **264:** it sits at rank 3 while the proposal's "Not verified" list says audit 123's finding may already be closed. Verify it first. Don't spend a head slot on it until the finding is confirmed open.
- **232:** the incident was a seat opening UI on the product owner's machine. I would move it ahead of the rename (rank 5), or at least ahead of rank 8.

Support-it

I can work under this order. The head bugs (290, 230, 264, 217) are the ones that change what my red, green and gate results mean. The guard that caps the head at four bugs and requires a failing check, reproduction or incident is clear, and I can follow it without gaming it.

Two things I would change:
- **"Every story" experiments (235, 256, 078, 072, 069, 139, 233):** these are seven obligations on every card. The no-burying guard says each must be "taken up or dropped" at the retro. Cap how many can be live on one card, say three, or the slice limit will be squeezed.
- **264 at rank 3:** it is conditional on a verification that has not happened. Move the check ahead of the Decider outcome, or time-box it, so a dev does not start it blind.

The retro log and the closures look fair.
